symptom: Custom chart `eventDataAttribute: EventData` inside a data view over page parameter $Entry (ChartEntry has no EventData) passes `check --references` and `exec`, then mx check reports `[CE1613] "The selected attribute 'MyFirstModule.ChartEntry.EventData' no longer exists."`; written qualified as MyFirstModule.ChartContext.EventData it is stored as such, but `describe page` prints `eventDataAttribute: EventData` and re-running that rebinds it to ChartEntry
cause: (1) misboundAttributeError refused a bare name only when ANOTHER entity in scope declared it, and returned nil for a name no entity had ("a plain typo, which other checks own") — no check owned it for pluggable properties; (2) extractExplicitProperties shortened every AttributeRef with describeAttr and was given no scope, and dataSourceEntityContext returned a parameter source's NAME (`Entry`) as the context entity, so no consumer could compare it to the attribute's entity
insight: A guard that stays quiet on the case it cannot place should say which check owns that case — this one named none, and grep found none. The describe half was the same mistake dataSourceEntityContext had already fixed twice (a flow's name, an association's name standing in for the entity): a parameter source stores its entity beside the name (`EntityRef.Entity` on Forms$DataViewSource), so it is read, not looked up from the page's parameters. To force the fault into a build, use a pre-fix binary: exec shares the refusal with check, so `--no-check` no longer writes the broken binding. Remaining: the stored qualified binding without a SourceVariable gets CE7247 from mx check in a fresh app; Studio Pro's page-parameter binding carries a Forms$PageVariable, which MDL still cannot spell for a pluggable attribute property
